text.p: Dollar/mark needs to vault back above 1.87 and hit a key retracement level to ensure a lasting rebound from the recent low set on Friday, technicians said on Tuesday.
They noted that 1.8710 marks corresponds to the 62-percent retracement of the slide from 1.8913 -- the near eight-year high set on Wednesday -- to 1.8385, the low on Friday.
Meanwhile, dollar/yen retraced only 38 percent of the slide from last week's high/low move from 119.58 to 114.25.
The smaller rebound may indicate an upcoming decoupling of dollar/mark and dollar/yen, the chartists said.

"Obviously, the breakdown in dollar/yen is more negative than in dollar/mark," said technical analyst Ben Morden at I.D.E.A. "The correction may be healthy for dollar/mark. It's building new momentum for another run at 1.89."
Morden, however, warned that another failure around 1.8913 marks would clearly indicate a double top and spell the end of the dollar's rally against Europe's continental currencies.

"A double top on the short-term charts at 1.89 marks would be very negative. But a break of the 1.89/1.90-mark area would strengthen the view that we are going to 2.0 marks," stressed Morden, referring to a level not seen since September 1989.
"I'm still bullish on dollar/mark but I see a divergence developing on dollar/yen," added Morden who said that pair may be in "a fifth-wave-type selling toward 115.40."
But Morden did not rule out a retreat all the way to 114.00 yen due to weakness in mark/yen where 61.90 support may be giving way which would weigh heavily on dollar/yen.
"The chart there is very bearish, we may go all the way to 61.50," Morden further predicted.
Another currency that has performed poorly lately is sterling that pulled back nearly 18 pfennigs from its July high at 3.08885 marks.
The longer-term outlook for either the dollar or sterling may be heavily influenced by the interplay between dollar/mark and sterling/mark, chartists also said.
A dollar/mark rally would likely prop up sterling/mark anew. However, fresh mark gains versus sterling may prevent an extended dollar/mark rebound, they noted.
Mark/Swiss is another cross that may signal the future trend of dollar/mark, mainly if important support at 0.8150 or even 0.8120 gives way.
